visual_text: One side effect, one extra drug
Calcium channel blocker started (for example amlodipine)
Ankle swelling: a known side effect
Illustrative example: a further drug for the diuretic's effects
Review the first drug: lower dose, switch, or stop if no longer needed
Loop diuretic within 3 months, people 66+ in Ontario: 14 per 1,000 after a calcium channel blocker; 7 per 1,000 after an ACE inhibitor or ARB
Dispensing data: shows who got a diuretic, not why
Savage et al., JAMA Intern Med 2020; Makani et al., J Hypertens 2011
alt_text: Diagram of a prescribing cascade. A calcium channel blocker such as amlodipine is started, ankle swelling follows as a known side effect, and a loop diuretic is added. A dashed box shows an illustrative further drug. Advice: review the first drug. In Ontario, people 66+ given a diuretic within 3 months: 14 per 1,000 after a calcium channel blocker, 7 per 1,000 after an ACE inhibitor or ARB.
design_instructions: Single card, light ground. H1 with em. Vertical flow: deep teal box (CCB started), mint box (ankle swelling), dashed mint box (loop diuretic), dashed grey box (illustrative further drug), orange-outlined review box, then two horizontal bars via barChart 14 (orange) vs 7 (teal) per 1,000. Claim C06-18-a. Source line Savage 2020; Makani 2011.
